sources.entry: An integrated library system is an enterprise resource planning system for a library, used to track items owned, orders made, bills paid, and patrons who have borrowed.

summary.name: Integrated library system
summary.one_liner: An integrated library system (ILS), also called a library management system (LMS), is an enterprise resource planning system for libraries that tracks owned items, orders, invoices, and patron borrowing.
summary.what_it_does: The page is a Wikipedia overview of integrated library systems. It describes an ILS as typically made of a relational database, software to interact with it, and staff and patron interfaces, split into modules such as acquisitions, cataloging, circulation, serials, and the OPAC. It traces the history from punch-card circulation in the 1930s through MARC-based bibliographic services, 1970s turnkey systems, web-based OPACs in the 1990s and 2000s, and the later rise of open-source and cloud systems. It includes a comparison table of open-source ILS platforms (Koha, PMB, NewGenLib, Evergreen, OpenBiblio, SLiMS) with their languages, licenses and release years.
notable: Modular design with acquisitions, cataloging, circulation, serials and OPAC modules
Comparison table of open-source ILS platforms with languages and licenses
Historical overview from 1930s punch cards to cloud-based systems
caveats: Describes a category of software rather than a single product; the page does not name one tool to install.
